jobs.title: Software Engineer II – Asset Management
jobs.description: COMPANY OVERVIEW We exist to make food the world loves. But we do more than that. Our company is a place that prioritizes being a force for good, a place to expand learning, explore new perspectives and reimagine new possibilities, every day. We look for people who want to bring their best — bold thinkers with big hearts who challenge one another and grow together. Because becoming the undisputed leader in food means surrounding ourselves with people who are hungry for what’s next. OVERVIEW The Sitecore Content Hub Developer will be part of a product team responsible for designing, developing, configuring, integrating, and supporting enterprise digital asset and content management capabilities on Sitecore Content Hub.The role will work closely with product owners, business analysts, solution architects, platform engineers, and other technology teams to translate business requirements into scalable Sitecore Content Hub solutions. The individual will provide technical leadership to developers, guide implementation decisions, participate in design and code reviews, and support the platform through delivery and production operations. The role requires strong experience with Sitecore Content Hub, digital asset management concepts, content models, workflows, metadata, integrations, and software engineering practices. The person will also contribute to platform modernization, automation, performance improvements, and continuous improvement initiatives. KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES Project Participation Participate in the complete software development lifecycle, from requirements and solution design through deployment and support. Analyze business and technical requirements and translate them into Sitecore Content Hub solutions. Configure and develop Content Hub entities, schemas, taxonomies, metadata models, policies, workflows, actions, and user roles. Design and implement integrations between Sitecore Content Hub and enterprise systems using REST APIs, webhooks, middleware, and event-driven patterns. Develop and maintain custom extensions, scripts, automations, and platform configurations where appropriate. Contribute to technical design documents, architecture discussions, sprint planning, and task-level estimation. Perform technical design reviews and ensure solutions align with enterprise standards and security requirements. Conduct code reviews and ensure maintainable, reusable, and standards-compliant code. Lead or contribute to deployment, release, environment promotion, and configuration management activities. Troubleshoot production issues, perform root-cause analysis, and implement sustainable fixes. Monitor and improve application and integration performance, reliability, and scalability. Collaborate with other teams to identify dependencies, manage risks, and resolve technical issues. Manage multiple workstreams while maintaining quality and delivery commitments. Provide application support on a rotation basis, including on-call support where required. Learning and Development Stay current with Sitecore Content Hub capabilities, product releases, DAM practices, integration patterns, and relevant industry trends. Mentor and coach team members to build technical depth and platform expertise. Drive process improvements at the project and team level. Lead knowledge-sharing sessions, reading groups, demonstrations, and technical communities of practice. Participate in hiring, onboarding, and capability development activities. Continue to strengthen communication, collaboration, consulting, and leadership skills. Consulting Provide module and project effort estimates. Recommend technical solutions and explain trade-offs to stakeholders. Act as a Sitecore Content Hub technical subject-matter expert. Develop functional expertise in digital asset management, content operations, product information, or a related business domain. Serve as a liaison between business analysts, product owners, architects, and developers. Answer implementation questions and provide technical direction throughout delivery. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Full-Time Bachelors degree with minimum 7-10 years of total work experience. Demonstrated ability to build a work plan or contribute to a work plan appropriate to the role. Experience implementing small projects or contributing to medium- or large-scale enterprise technology projects. Hands-on experience with Sitecore Content Hub, preferably including Content Management, Digital Asset Management, Product Content Management, or related modules. Experience configuring Content Hub data models, schemas, taxonomies, relations, metadata, workflows, roles, permissions, and business rules. Experience with Sitecore Content Hub APIs, REST services, webhooks, integrations, and authentication mechanisms. Experience developing or configuring integrations with enterprise applications, cloud services, middleware, or data platforms. Strong understanding of DAM concepts, including asset lifecycle management, renditions, versioning, metadata governance, rights management, and content distribution. Proficiency in object-oriented programming and at least one modern programming language such as C#, JavaScript, or TypeScript. Working knowledge of .NET, ASP.NET Core, Web API, SQL, JSON, XML, and HTTP-based services. Experience with source control, CI/CD, automated testing, deployment practices, and Agile delivery. Good working knowledge of the enterprise application and technical tools landscape. Ability to proactively resolve issues, take ownership, and work across multiple tasks and teams. Ability to become a go-to resource for the team or business group. Experience with third-party integrations and enterprise system interfaces. Provide senior-level technical leadership by shaping designs, reviewing code, strengthening engineering standards, collaborating across product and technology teams, and advising business partners. Design, develop, and support scalable Sitecore Content Hub capabilities for the reliable management and organization of digital assets and product content. Configure and extend Content Hub data models, schemas, taxonomies, relationships, metadata, workflows, roles, permissions, and business rules to support effective content governance. Design and maintain integrations between Content Hub and enterprise applications, cloud services, middleware, data platforms, and third-party systems, using Azure Functions, Logic Apps, API Management, messaging/event-driven services, or equivalent technologies. Develop solutions using object-oriented programming and modern practices with technologies such as C#, .NET, ASP.NET Core, Web API, JavaScript, TypeScript, SQL, JSON, and XML. Apply DAM expertise across the asset lifecycle, including renditions, versioning, rights management, content quality, and distribution. Build secure, maintainable services using Content Hub APIs, REST, webhooks, authentication mechanisms, and other HTTP-based interfaces. Establish and execute quality-engineering practices, including unit, integration, automated, performance, and regression testing, supported by effective CI/CD and deployment processes. Deliver initiatives across the full software-development lifecycle, contribute to medium- and large-scale enterprise projects, and resolve production issues through root-cause analysis and durable fixes. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Sitecore Content Hub certification or formal Sitecore training. Experience with Sitecore XM Cloud, Sitecore Experience Platform, or other Sitecore products. Experience with Sitecore Content Hub One, Content Operations, or DAM platform migration. Experience with product information management, product data, or master data concepts. Experience with cloud platforms such as Azure or GCP. Experience with Azure Functions, Logic Apps, API Management, messaging platforms, or equivalent integration services. Experience with DevOps tooling, infrastructure automation, observability, and application monitoring. Familiarity with accessibility, security, privacy, and enterprise content governance standards. Experience with performance testing, unit testing, automated integration testing, and quality engineering. Experience working with global, distributed, and cross-functional teams. ELIGIBILITY Applicants must meet minimum age qualifications in the country in which the job is located.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer III, PaySec, StoreSec
jobs.description: DESCRIPTION Come build the future with us! In Payments Security (PaySec), we protect the foundational systems and products that allow Amazon to accept payments for all goods, content, and services that people buy at Amazon and around the world. International Emerging Stores Payments (IESP) brings Amazon's payments products to customers in some of the fastest-growing markets in the world, across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), Asia Pacific (APAC) including India, and South America. These markets run on real-time payment rails such as UPI, on local wallets, cards, bill payments, and lending products, and on regulatory regimes that differ from one country to the next. Every one of those transactions depends on customer trust, and IESP Payments Security exists to earn and keep it. Payments Security owns full-stack Product Security for Payments across Amazon and its business units. We are part of Amazon's broader Stores Security organization, responsible for protecting Amazon's global information assets. We partner with Payments builder teams to make applications and infrastructure secure-by-design from concept to launch and into continuous operations, and we build the mechanisms, guardrails, and automation that let thousands of engineers do the right thing by default. As a software engineer on IESP Payments Security, you will build the software that makes security automatic for Amazon's payments businesses in MENA, APAC including India, and South America. Imagine writing the code that stops a vulnerability before it is merged, or an AI agent that scans hundreds of production applications and finds payment data stored where it should not be. You will work on three kinds of problems. First, controls-as-code: security rules and guardrails that run on every code change, including code written with AI assistance. Second, detection agents: AI-assisted services that find sensitive data, vulnerable patterns, and risky configurations across production. Third, onboarding acquired stacks: tooling that brings newly acquired businesses onto Amazon's standard engineering and security platforms. You will work side by side with security engineers, and your work will show up directly in fewer vulnerabilities and less time builders spend fixing them. As a senior engineer, you will set the technical direction for the team's systems, lead designs that span multiple components and teams, and mentor other engineers. Key job responsibilities Lead the architecture and technical direction of the team's security tooling, and make trade-offs between precision, coverage, latency, and builder experience. Design, build, test, deploy, and operate secure, highly available services that handle sensitive payments data. Build controls-as-code and code-creation security rules that catch common vulnerability patterns before code is merged. Build AI-assisted detection agents that find sensitive payment data and vulnerable code patterns across production applications, with high precision. Build tooling that onboards acquired businesses' code, cloud accounts, and pipelines onto Amazon's standard security tooling. Build automated remediation that proposes or writes the fix for a finding, not just flags it, so builders spend minutes instead of days. Meet directly with security engineers and service teams to understand their requirements, and design solutions that make them more productive. Estimate engineering effort, plan implementation, and roll out changes that meet requirements for performance, scalability, and reliability. Work with security engineers to turn threat models and findings into automated mechanisms. Contribute to operational excellence through code reviews, testing, monitoring, and on-call. Lead designs that span multiple teams, including integration with Amazon's central security and developer platforms. Work with stakeholders to gather and document requirements, and take part in strategic planning for the team's roadmap. Grow and coach engineers on the team, and raise the bar in design and code reviews. A day in the life You will spend most of your time building: designing services, writing and reviewing code, and shipping. You will pair with security engineers who bring a threat model or a class of findings, and together you will decide what can be automated and how to measure that it works. You will meet the service teams who use our tools, hear where security slows them down, and fix it. The team runs regular architecture reviews and knowledge shares, and you will learn security from people who do it every day. About the team IESP Payments Security is a single-threaded Business Security Team for all of International Emerging Stores Payments. We are security engineers, technical program managers, and software engineers working as one team. We own security for regulated payments and lending businesses, for acquired companies joining Amazon, and for new markets as they launch. We believe security scales through mechanisms and automation, not headcount. As AI writes more of the code our builders ship, we move security into the moment code is created and replace episodic reviews with continuous assurance. We invest in each other's growth as much as we invest in protecting our customers. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS 5+ years of non-internship professional software development experience 5+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience 5+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 8+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent Experience developing and delivering security software tools Expertise in security and permission management systems, such as AWS IAM and AWS Organizations. Experience building with large language models or AI agents in production. Proven programming ability in Java, C++, Python, Go, TypeScript, or related. Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

jobs.title: Sr Serviceability Engineer - Life Cycle Manager (LCM)
jobs.description: About Nutanix Nutanix is building a world where infrastructure is invisible, and organizations can focus on the work that matters. Our hybrid multicloud platform helps customers run applications and manage data across private, public, and distributed clouds with simplicity and control. About the Team The Serviceability Engineer role is part of the Service Strategy & Enablement team at Nutanix, based in Bangalore. The team is made up of engineers who improve product serviceability, diagnostics, reliability, and the overall customer experience. Serving as a critical bridge between Support and Engineering, the team ensures that serviceability and usability are considered throughout the product lifecycle. By analyzing customer issues, monitoring field performance, validating releases, and incorporating customer feedback, the team drives improvements that make Nutanix products easier to deploy, upgrade, troubleshoot, and operate. You will report to the Manager, Service Strategy & Enablement. The team works in a hybrid environment that encourages collaboration, technical learning, and ownership. Your Role As a Senior Serviceability Engineer for Life Cycle Manager (LCM) , you will help make upgrades predictable, diagnosable, and safe across Nutanix software and hardware environments. You will work closely with Engineering, Product Management, Quality Assurance, Release Management, and Support to improve the serviceability of LCM from product definition through release and post-deployment adoption. LCM provides a cluster-aware framework for inventorying and updating software and firmware across a Nutanix environment. This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys understanding complex distributed systems, investigating customer-impacting failures, improving product diagnostics, and influencing teams to prevent recurring issues. The role involves performing duties requiring the application of professional expertise and the exercise of independent judgment/discretion, creativity, problem-solving, and decision-making in carrying out responsibilities, as applicable to the position. The specific responsibilities of the role may vary based on business needs and role requirements. Employees can refer to the applicable guidelines and career frameworks for additional information regarding role expectations and responsibilities. What You’ll Do Define and maintain serviceability requirements for LCM features, upgrade workflows, inventory, prechecks, compatibility validation, recovery, and diagnostics. Partner with Product Management and Engineering during product planning and development to ensure customer troubleshooting and operational needs are addressed early. Lead serviceability validation for LCM releases, including upgrade-path testing, upgrade and inventory workflows, precheck coverage, failure and recovery scenarios, interoperability, scale, and upgrade resiliency. Build and maintain representative test matrices across Nutanix software, hypervisors, server platforms, firmware components, cluster configurations, and supported deployment models. Review field issues, support cases, telemetry, and diagnostic data to identify trends, customer impact, recurring failure modes, and opportunities for product improvement. Investigate complex LCM failures by correlating application logs, task and workflow data, cluster state, system events, network behavior, and firmware or hardware-management responses. Work with Engineering to isolate root causes, reproduce issues, define corrective actions, and drive critical and deferred defects to closure. Review precheck and compatibility behavior to ensure that failures are actionable, accurately classified, and supported by clear remediation guidance. Evaluate upgrade rollback, recovery, and partial-failure scenarios and help define safe customer outcomes when an upgrade does not complete as expected. Collaborate with Quality Assurance and test automation teams to improve coverage for upgrade paths, dependency conflicts, hardware variants, network conditions, disconnected or restricted environments, and negative scenarios. Partner with Release Management and Documentation teams on release readiness, known issues, upgrade guidance, troubleshooting content, and Support enablement. Translate complex technical findings into clear requirements, defect reports, troubleshooting guides, executive summaries, and customer-safe recommendations. Represent the customer and Support perspective in design reviews, technical discussions, defect triage, and release decisions. Mentor engineers and promote serviceability practices that reduce customer effort, support case volume, time to resolution, and avoidable upgrade risk. What You’ll Bring 5+ years of experience in enterprise software, platform engineering, systems engineering, quality engineering, technical support, or serviceability. Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline; equivalent practical experience will also be considered. Experience working with complex infrastructure products, distributed systems, virtualization platforms, cloud infrastructure, or data-center operations. Strong experience troubleshooting customer-impacting issues across multiple layers of a technology stack and converting investigation findings into durable product improvements. Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence Engineering, Product Management, Quality, and Support without relying solely on formal authority. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with engineers, technical support teams, product leaders, and executive stakeholders. Technical Requirements Life Cycle Management and Upgrade Workflows Strong understanding of software and firmware lifecycle management, including inventory, repositories, package or bundle management, prechecks, dependencies, compatibility, upgrade sequencing, and post-upgrade validation. Experience testing or troubleshooting upgrade workflows involving failure handling, partial completion, recovery, retry, and resumption scenarios. Understanding of the operational risks associated with infrastructure upgrades and the importance of clear customer-facing diagnostics and remediation guidance. Virtualization and Nutanix Technologies Hands-on experience with one or more virtualization or hypervisor technologies, such as Nutanix AHV/KVM or VMware ESXi. Familiarity with enterprise infrastructure concepts such as clusters, controllers, virtual machines, storage, networking, high availability, and rolling maintenance. Experience with Nutanix technologies such as AOS, Prism, AHV, or LCM is a plus. Systems and Infrastructure Troubleshooting Strong Linux administration and troubleshooting skills, including process, service, filesystem, permissions, networking, and system-resource analysis. Ability to analyze logs, task histories, service states, configuration files, alerts, and diagnostic bundles to identify failure patterns. Familiarity with server hardware, firmware, boot processes, out-of-band management, and hardware-management interfaces such as Redfish or IPMI is preferred. Understanding of network fundamentals relevant to infrastructure upgrades, including DNS, routing, firewalls, proxies, TLS certificates, repositories, and connectivity validation. Automation, APIs, and Diagnostics Proficiency in Python, Shell, or another scripting language for test automation, log analysis, data extraction, and operational tooling. Experience working with REST APIs, JSON, authentication, error handling, and API-driven infrastructure workflows. Familiarity with observability, telemetry, log collection, diagnostic bundles, and metrics used to detect and troubleshoot product issues. Experience building or improving automated validation for upgrade, compatibility, failure-injection, or recovery scenarios. Serviceability and Quality Engineering Experience defining test strategies, test plans, acceptance criteria, release gates, and validation metrics for complex products. Proven ability to review and prioritize defects using customer impact, frequency, severity, reproducibility, and business risk. Ability to create high-quality defect reports with clear symptoms, impact, reproduction steps, evidence, suspected scope, and validation criteria. Experience using tools such as Jira, Confluence, or equivalent systems for defect tracking, documentation, and cross-functional execution. Experience using AI to automate workflows, build task-oriented agents, or analyze defects, bugs, and diagnostic data. Preferred Qualifications Experience with infrastructure lifecycle management, firmware orchestration, server vendors, or data-center management platforms. Experience supporting or validating air-gapped, dark-site, proxy-based, or restricted-network environments. Knowledge of upgrade compatibility models, dependency graphs, release branches, backward compatibility, and interoperability testing. Experience with CI/CD, test frameworks, continuous validation, or quality dashboards. Background in technical support, escalation engineering, site reliability engineering, or customer-facing engineering for enterprise infrastructure products. Experience creating technical documentation, knowledge base content, troubleshooting guides, or Support readiness material. Why This Role Matters Infrastructure upgrades are high-trust operations for customers. In this role, you will help ensure that LCM does more than execute an upgrade: it should explain what is happening, identify risks early, recover safely when conditions change, and give customers and Support a clear path to resolution. If you enjoy solving difficult infrastructure problems, working across product boundaries, and turning field experience into better engineering outcomes, this is an opportunity to have a direct impact on the reliability and usability of Nutanix products. Nutanix is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.
